title: Maximal Score After Applying K Operations
statement:
You begin with a score of `0` and an integer array `nums`. A single operation chooses any index `i`, adds the current value `nums[i]` to the score, and then overwrites `nums[i]` with `ceil(nums[i] / 3)` (one third, rounded up to an integer).

Perform exactly `k` operations; the same index may be chosen as many times as you like. Return the largest total score you can finish with.
notes:
## Intuition

Every operation adds the chosen value to the score and only shrinks that one value, so the other values are untouched. Taking the current largest value is never worse: it gains the most now, and because `ceil(x / 3)` never shrinks as `x` grows, it also leaves behind at least as large a value for later. Rescanning the array for the maximum each time costs O(n·k); a max-heap hands over the largest value in O(log n).

## Approach

1. Copy `nums` into `heap` and turn it into a max-heap by sifting down every internal node, from the last one back to the root.
2. Repeat `k` times: add the root `heap[0]` to `score`, replace it with `Math.ceil(heap[0] / 3)`, and sift it down so the largest value returns to the root.
3. Return `score`.

`siftDown` compares a node with its `left` and `right` children, swaps it with the `largest`, and continues from there until the node is bigger than both children.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [10,10,10,10,10]`, `k = 5`. The root is 10: score 10, it becomes 4 and sinks. The next root is another 10, and so on: after five operations every 10 has been taken once, the heap holds five 4s, and `score = 50`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + k log n): building the heap is linear, and each operation sifts once.
- Space: O(n) for the copy of the array.

## Pitfalls

- Round **up**: `ceil(10 / 3)` is 4, not 3. Plain integer division gives the wrong score.
- The score can reach about 10^14, beyond 32-bit range; Java and C need a 64-bit total.
- Values never drop below 1, so even a huge `k` keeps adding at least 1 per operation.
- Replacing the root in place avoids a separate pop and push.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `heap` | max-heap of the current values |
| `siftDown` | restores the heap order below `index` |
| `left`, `right` | children positions of `index` |
| `largest` | position of the largest of the node and its children |
| `score` | total gained so far |
| `op` | number of operations done |
